data.name: GeometryDashboard_HelpText
data.value:
This tool derives virtual points, lines, and circles from the hit objects in your editor and overlays them on the editor. Use a hotkey to snap your cursor to this geometry while mapping. Hotkeys also let you select, lock, and control whether virtual objects can be used by generators. Configure the hotkeys and other options in Preferences. Hover over labels for more information.
Virtual objects are generated in layers: the first layer contains the editor's hit objects; each following layer contains virtual objects derived from the previous layer. Set the number of layers in Preferences. Additional layers can produce many more virtual objects.
The generator list below creates virtual objects from hit objects or other virtual objects. Basic generators use hit objects as input and show results immediately. Advanced generators use virtual objects as input, so at least one basic generator must be active first. Use Configure on a generator to change its input selection or output settings.
Savestates let you switch between preference and generator configurations using hotkeys. Open them with the button beside Preferences.
To use this tool, set your osu! user configuration file in Mapping Tools Preferences (Options → Preferences).
data.comment: Help text opened from the Geometry Dashboard header. Explain virtual geometry overlays, hotkeys, layer generation, basic and advanced generators, generator configuration, savestates, and the required osu! user configuration. Geometry Dashboard, Mapping Tools, osu!, and Savestates are product or feature names and must remain unchanged in translations.

data.value:
Sliderator is a tool meant to make sliders with variable velocity. That means sliders that change speed during the animation. You can also make variable velocity streams with this tool.
The UI consists of a slider import section, some options, a position/velocity graph, and a slider preview.
To get started, simply import one or more sliders using the 'Import sliders' button. Use any of the three different import methods from the dropdown menu.
The most important element is the position/velocity graph. This is where you tell Sliderator what you want your slider animation to look like. You can toggle between position and velocity mode by clicking the accent colored button below. Add, remove, or edit anchors with right click and move stuff by dragging with left click. While dragging, hold Shift for horizontal clipping, hold Ctrl for vertical clipping, and hold Alt to disable snapping.
Running Sliderator with a constant velocity will give back the original slider. You can manually choose a lower SV and bigger tumour length to optimise your slider.
Check out all the options. The tooltips should help you further.

data.name: TumourGenerator_Help
data.comment: Help text explaining layered tumour generation on sliders, shape/size/placement controls, advanced time-varying parameters, arrow-key fine adjustment, and preview/run workflow. Preserve “Preview slider” as the button caption when translating elsewhere.
data.value: Tumour Generator 2 generates copious amounts of tumours on sliders. You can adjust the shape and size of tumours and choose where they should be placed along the path. You can also generate multiple layers of tumours. A layer will either merge the tumours with the tumours of the previous layer or place the tumours on top of the previous tumours. Enable the Advanced toggle and click the ... button to edit how a parameter changes over time. Use the arrow keys on the sliders to do fine adjustments. To get started, select a slider in your beatmap and click 'Preview slider' to preview changes or click the run button to instantly generate tumours on the selected sliders.
